title: Conservative surge mitigation checklist and operator notes (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an operational-first checklist and set of field notes for handling short-duration traffic surges during cross-functional rollouts (canaries, micro-A/Bs, feature gates). Focus: minimize user-visible latency spikes and runaway cost, preserve safety gates, and keep rollback decisions simple for on-call.

Quick TL;DR for an oncall or steward:
- If latency spikes but error rate steady -> throttle by slice, reduce batch windows, enable low-latency routing.
- If quality regressions or hallucinations -> immediate slice quarantine + partial rollback to prior model variant; escalate to product owning team.
- If token usage/cost blowup observed -> flip cost-quota circuit (auto-rewrite to lower-temp model), alert Finance+GTM.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers; private deployments may have different knobs (local KMS, firewall).
- Assumes traffic is partitioned into slices (e.g., by cohort, region, platform).
- We assume Console exposes per-slice throttles, routing policies, and model-variant fallbacks.

Operational checklist (prioritized):
1) Early detection (first 0-3 minutes)
   - Check: per-slice 1m P95 latency, 1m error rate, token/sec for top 5 slices.
   - Action: If top-1 slice accounts for >40% of unexpected token growth, enable slice isolation (route new traffic to neutral bucket).
   - Note: Cheap signal: token/sec bump with no error rate rise often means more verbose user prompts or a client bug.

2) Short-term controls (3-15 minutes)
   - Throttle: reduce requests/sec by 20-50% on offending slice. Use gradual ramp-down with 10s windows to avoid oscillation.
   - Model fallback: enable cheapest compatible model variant for new requests (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant). Do not migrate in-flight requests.
   - Batch tuning: lower max_batch_bytes / max_tokens_in_batch for low-latency SLOs.
   - Circuit for embeddings/rerankers: if embeddings cost skyrockets, switch to cached results for 1% traffic and increase sampling.

3) Medium-term controls (15-90 minutes)
   - Canary rollback: if A/B metric delta beyond tolerance (see gating math below), revert cohort to baseline model.
   - Progressive re-enable: after rollback, re-enable 5% -> 20% -> 100% slices only after 30m stability windows.
   - Billing throttle: enforce per-customer token cap for shared-hosted tenants; notify account owner.

4) Incident playbook (when to page / escalate)
   - Page SRE + Product if any of: sustained P99 latency >2x baseline for >15m, error rate spike >3x baseline, quality score regression (automatic eval) > threshold.
   - Page ML/Applied if hallucination/classifier-drift signals present.
   - Page Sales/CS + Finance if customer cost exceed committed by >25% in 1h.

Gating math (simple heuristics for steward decisions):
- Minimum detectable uplift (binary metric) for cohort size n: delta_min = 1.96 * sqrt(p*(1-p)/n) where p is baseline success rate. Use p=0.98 for availability.
- Example: for n=2000 impressions, delta_min ~ 0.0096 (0.96%). If observed delta > 3x delta_min -> treat as substantive.
- Latency cost tradeoff: rough token cost elasticity = d(cost)/d(latency) approximated by batch size * token_rate. If latency cut reduces batch size by 30% expect cost +15-25% (hand-wave — measure).

Design notes / reasoning (why conservative?):
- Surges often driven by client changes or outbound campaign; conservatism avoids false rollbacks that hide true regressions.
- Aim for human-in-loop for final rollback decisions; automatic reverts only for hard safety signals (e.g., policy violations, runaway cost alarms).

Example scenarios & preferred actions (field notes):
- Scenario A: sudden spike in verbose prompts from mobile SDK after a client release.
  - Signal: token/sec up 5x, latency +25% P95, error rate flat.
  - Action: reduce throttle on mobile slice to 70% traffic, enable cached prefix responses where possible, spin up extra dedicated capacity if SLA requires it, notify SDK owner.

- Scenario B: A/B shows small but consistent drift in sentiment for new model variant.
  - Signal: sentiment metric down 4% vs baseline over 6 hours, traffic evenly distributed.
  - Action: quarantine cohort, failover to old variant, run local eval on triggered sample, schedule postmortem if regression confirmed.

- Scenario C: rogue reranker causing token amplification (cascade with generation layer).
  - Signal: embeddings calls per session jump 3x and generation tokens up 2x; cost spikes.
  - Action: enable embeddings cache + synthetic fallback routing to stub reranker, throttle downstream generation, page applied-ml and infra.

Human ops scripts (copyable snippets stewards can run):
- Isolate slice (Console API): POST /v1/traffic/actions {"slice":"mobile-ios-v2","action":"isolate"} -- comment: isolates new traffic to neutral bucket.
- Enable model fallback: POST /v1/models/routing {"slice":"X","fallback_variant":"small-q8"} -- comment: affects only new requests.
- Throttle by pct: PATCH /v1/slices/mobile {"incoming_pct":70} -- watch for oscillations.

Monitoring checklist for 1st hour after any mitigation:
- 1m/5m P95 + P99, slabbed by slice and model variant.
- token/sec by slice and by model variant.
- cost burn rate (USD/hr) and estimated 24h burn.
- qualitative: sample 100 responses from affected cohort, check for safety signals, hallucinations, regressed formatting.

Open questions / debate items (to resolve in product guild):
- Auto-revert policy: should we auto-revert for cost-only signals? pros/cons. (My leaning: no auto-revert, only throttle/circuit).
- Guardrail taxonomy: unify "cost" vs "latency" vs "quality" in a single severity score? How to weight user-facing impact vs vendor cost?
- Sampling cadence: what's the right response sample size for near-real-time quality checks without costly instrumentation? 250-500/day?

Backlog actionable items (next steps):
- [ ] Add a per-slice cost-forecast widget in Console (owner: Jonas).
- [ ] Ship an operator 'isolate slice' button with circuit breaker confirmation (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add synthetic traffic harness that can model token amplification chains (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Document exact metric thresholds for paging in SLO runbook (owner: Maya).

Notes-to-self: keep this conservative and low-automation. Prefer clear human intent over automatic heuristics until we have >6 months of labeled incidents.

References / useful links:
- Related runbooks: SRG-42 (linked above), rollout gating notes in Confluence.
- Debrief template for rollbacks: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-templates/rollback-debrief.md

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
